asDecan.p: Every sign gets split into three ten-degree pieces, called decans, and each piece gets a planet of its own. Your Sun falls somewhere between ten and nineteen degrees of Pisces, the middle slice, and the Golden Dawn hands that slice to Jupiter. As these things go, that's a lucky match. Jupiter is the traditional ruler of Pisces, so here it's at home and doesn't have to try very hard, and the middle of any sign is where the sign is most settled into itself. Pisces is mutable water, feeling that moves and takes the shape of whatever it's poured into. The slice before yours belongs to Saturn and the Eight of Cups, the figure walking away from a row of cups at night. The slice after goes to Mars and the Ten, which has a bit more push in it. Yours sits between the leaving and the building, in the part that's simply full. The Moon is your Sun card, being the Major for Pisces, and the Nine is the finer grain inside it.

You're usually the most relaxed person at the table, and people pick up on it before they could say why. At a family dinner where two cousins are circling an old row, you're the one refilling glasses, and somehow the evening stays fine. A friend sends a long anxious message at eleven at night and you answer it properly, with a voice note, because it didn't occur to you to leave it till morning. On a Sunday with nothing planned you don't feel guilty at all. You go to the market, buy too much bread, and call it a good day. I see this a lot with mid-Pisces Suns. There's a baseline of feeling okay that other people have to work quite hard for. You'd probably say you've just been lucky, and some of it is Jupiter being comfortable where it sits, which does tend to look like luck from the outside.

The less obvious gift is that you can take a good thing when it's handed to you. Plenty of people can't. Someone offers to cover dinner, or your manager says the report was excellent, and most people deflect, or start paying it back in their heads straight away. You say thanks, mean it, and order the dessert. That sounds small, but it gives everyone around you permission to do the same. At a birthday where the person being celebrated is squirming, you're the one who makes it easy for them to sit there and be fussed over. Jupiter in its own sign trusts that there's enough to go round, and you carry that into rooms where people are quietly counting.

The trickier side is that being content can slide into not looking. If things feel fine, you'd honestly rather not check. The bank statement stays unopened because the month felt okay. A friendship has gone a bit one-sided and you keep telling yourself it's lovely, because the alternative is a conversation, and conversations like that make you feel slightly ill. Have a look at the man on the card, sitting with his arms folded in front of all those cups. He's pleased, and he's also a bit shut. You can be like that too, a little smug about how well things are going, in a way that makes it hard for someone to tell you they're struggling right beside you. Pisces goes around obstacles easily. Sometimes the obstacle needed looking at.

When something goes wrong, a redundancy, a death, a partner leaving, your first move is usually to make everyone else feel better. You're organising the food after the funeral, reassuring your mum, telling friends you're honestly fine. For a few days that's even true. About a week later it tends to leak out sideways, through comfort. A bottle of wine most nights where there used to be a glass, takeaway four nights running, a spend on something nice you tell yourself you've earned. Jupiter at home expands whatever it touches, and that includes the soothing. The people around you often don't realise anything's wrong, which has its own cost, because they never get the chance to look after you back. What helps is letting one person see it. Tell them it's bad, in those words, and let them bring the food for once.

Where it gets interesting is who you tend to fall for. With this much warmth to spare, you're often drawn to someone a bit lost, the one at the party who's had a rough year and lights up when you listen. That can be lovely for a while. It gets tiring when you notice you've become the whole source of their good mood, and they've stopped bringing much to the relationship apart from need. The ones that last for mid-Pisces people are usually with someone who's already fairly happy on their own, who has their own friends and their own Saturday plans. To be honest, that can feel a bit unromantic at first. Then you find there's someone filling your glass as well, and it's a very different life.

You do well in work where people come to you feeling worse and leave feeling better. Hospitality, nursing, teaching small children, running events, a café that's known for the owner as much as the coffee. Jupiter is also the planet of teaching and belief, so you're often the one who gets a team to think the thing can actually be done. Where you slip is detail and money. You'd sooner give the discount than chase the invoice, and you'll agree to an extra project because it sounds fun, then find it's due the same week as three others. A manager who handles the numbers, or a business partner who's properly fussy about them, frees you to do what you're good at. Let them have the spreadsheet.

At twenty this often looks like being everyone's favourite person and having no money. You say yes to every night out, lend what you haven't got, and the good feeling carries you through most of it. By the mid-thirties there's usually been at least one stretch where the comfort went too far, a debt, a relationship you stayed in because it was pleasant enough, a habit you didn't much like. Most people with this slice sort it out without a lot of drama, because feeling well matters to them and they notice when they don't. The fifties tend to be good years for this decan. The contentment has had some knocks and it's sturdier for them, and people often find that the friends they were kind to at twenty-five are still around.

Once a month, pick an evening and look at your actual bank balance and your actual calendar together, with a cup of tea and nothing else on. Write down one thing you've been telling yourself is fine that you haven't checked. Just one. Then check it that week, whether it's the credit card, the friend you haven't heard from in a while, or the dentist you keep putting off. Most of the time it really is fine, and then you can enjoy it properly.
